interface.title: RobustPrint Virtual Lab
interface.field: Materials and process engineering: 3D printing (FDM) with recycled mixed-plastic feedstock
interface.stage_of_work: Experiment planning, surrogate modelling and process optimisation under feedstock uncertainty, all against a synthetic simulator
interface.what_it_is_for: Explore how batch-to-batch variation in recycled feedstock composition affects printed-part strength and print success, train a calibrated model on a campaign of print jobs, choose robust print settings, and propose the next experiments.

data.note: Most of the work ran on a simulated campaign generated in the browser (60 batches × 4 settings × 3 specimens = 240 jobs). I also uploaded example_experiments.csv (9 valid jobs, 6 of them failed prints with empty strength) and starter_design.csv. The design file was rejected because it has no outcome columns. Study results come from bundled pre-registered Python outputs.

tree.general: Find process settings that work reliably on a variable raw material, judge how sure you can be of the outcome and how much of that uncertainty comes from the material itself, and decide which experiments to run next
tree.specific: Choose FDM print settings that are robust to recycled-feedstock composition variation, using a learned GP strength model and success classifier; read how confident the predicted part strength is and what share of its uncertainty comes from feedstock; and plan the next print jobs

features.name: Uncertain-input distribution editor with live outcome preview

Adjust consistency κ to widen or narrow lot-to-lot spread (± SD shown beside each fraction)

features.name: Multiplicative loss waterfall

features.specific: 'Where the strength goes': blend strength × fibre × inclusions × degradation/hydrolysis × bonding × porosity × raster × infill × over-extrusion, with red losses and green gains and a mechanism tooltip on each factor
steps: Change an input (for example moisture or nozzle temperature)
Watch which factor bar grows
Hover a factor label for its mechanism

features.name: One-factor response curves with uncertainty bands

steps: Choose the variable to vary
Read where the median and band peak relative to the dashed current value
Hover for the value at a point
Change other settings and see the curves move

screens_never_reached: The Study results links (summary.csv, tests.csv, LIMITATIONS.md) and 'Source and study' point to github.com, outside the allowed server, so I did not open them.
not_done: I did not round-trip the copied CSV template back through import with real measured outcomes filled in. The browser has no file of my own to edit, and typing a full results file by hand was beyond the action budget.
I could not import starter_design.csv as a design to plan from: the importer requires outcome columns and rejected it. Only the built-in Latin-hypercube campaign covers that framing.
Thorough (3 000) search effort, the 300 and 2 000 fresh-batch options, and the 'Maximum uncertainty' and 'Space-filling' strategies were not tried, to save actions.
I trained the model only on the simulated campaign. With only the 9 imported example jobs (3 strengths; at least 5 are needed), Train model stayed disabled (screens/014.webp).
The Optimise form's checkboxes and dropdowns reverted to defaults after I navigated away and back, though the results stayed. I noted this but did not investigate further.
The run never kept a screen of E4 (uncertainty sources) on Study results; the replay found it only in the accessibility tree, below the screenshots.
